skill.name: e2e-testing-patterns
skill.description: Build reliable end-to-end test suites with Playwright and Cypress. Use this skill to plan user journeys, write stable selectors, debug flaky tests, and set CI standards.
skill.summary: Create reliable Playwright and Cypress E2E tests for critical user workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The flagged items are documentation examples for E2E testing, not executable skill logic. Backticks are JavaScript template strings or Markdown inline code, network calls target local or relative test routes, and environment variables are used for CI settings or example test credentials. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent.

remediation.issue: The admin credential example could be copied without enough context.
remediation.suggestion: State that ADMIN_PASSWORD must belong to a dedicated non-production test account and must never reference real production credentials.

remediation.issue: The request mutation example changes a user role during interception.
remediation.suggestion: Frame the role change as a controlled local test fixture and warn users not to run it against production or third-party systems.

content.value_statement: End-to-end tests often become slow, flaky, and hard to maintain. This skill gives Playwright and Cypress patterns for stable workflows, selectors, fixtures, debugging, and CI.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use E2E tests instead of unit or integration tests.
Provides Playwright configuration patterns for retries, traces, screenshots, video, and browser projects.
Shows page object, fixture, selector, waiting, and network interception patterns.
Provides Cypress configuration, custom commands, request helpers, and intercept examples.
Covers visual regression, sharding, accessibility scans, and debugging with traces and screenshots.
Lists common pitfalls and best practices for reliable selectors, cleanup, and independent tests.
limitations: It does not run tests or install Playwright, Cypress, or related packages by itself.
Examples must be adapted to each application's routes, data model, and authentication rules.
Some sample code uses placeholder credentials and local URLs that are not production-ready.
It does not replace unit, integration, accessibility, or security testing.

use_cases.title: Standardize Critical Journey Tests
use_cases.description: Define a focused E2E suite for login, checkout, signup, or other user journeys that must not regress.

use_cases.title: Debug Flaky UI Automation
use_cases.description: Replace fixed waits, brittle selectors, and shared state with deterministic waiting, stable locators, and isolated data.

use_cases.title: Prepare Browser Tests for CI
use_cases.description: Set retries, parallel execution, trace capture, browser projects, and artifacts for repeatable CI test runs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan My E2E Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this feature and identify the smallest useful E2E suite. Separate critical user journeys from cases better covered by unit or integration tests.

prompt_templates.title: Design Stable Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Playwright or Cypress tests for this workflow. Include selector strategy, test data setup, waiting strategy, cleanup, and failure artifacts.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Flaky Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these flaky E2E symptoms and suggest likely causes. Recommend concrete fixes for synchronization, selectors, shared data, network behavior, and CI variance.

prompt_templates.title: Create CI Browser Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an advanced E2E strategy for a multi-browser CI pipeline. Cover sharding, retries, trace collection, visual checks, accessibility scans, and release gates.

output_examples.input: I need E2E coverage for a checkout flow.
output: Prioritize one happy path, one payment failure path, and one cart update path.
Use stable user-facing selectors and create fresh test data before each test.
Capture traces and screenshots only on failure to keep CI output manageable.

output_examples.input: Our login tests fail randomly in CI.
output: Check for fixed waits, reused accounts, race conditions after submit, and missing network response assertions.
Use explicit URL or page state expectations after login.
Store CI traces and screenshots so each failure has enough diagnostic context.

output_examples.input: We want browser tests before every deployment.
output: Run a short smoke suite on every pull request and a broader suite before release.
Shard longer tests by browser or feature area.
Fail deployment only on critical journey regressions, not non-blocking visual differences.

best_practices: Choose a small set of critical journeys before writing browser tests.
Use user-facing selectors or stable data attributes, not DOM structure.
Keep test data isolated and capture traces, screenshots, and videos on failure.
anti_patterns: Testing every edge case through the browser instead of lower-level tests.
Using fixed sleeps, CSS chains, or nth-child selectors as primary synchronization.
Running destructive or credentialed tests against production systems.

faq.question: Does this skill support both Playwright and Cypress?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for Playwright configuration, Cypress configuration, selectors, fixtures, waits, intercepts, and debugging.

faq.question: Can it choose what should be tested with E2E?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps identify critical user journeys and separates E2E coverage from lower-level unit or integration coverage.

faq.question: Will it run tests for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and implementation guidance. You still need a configured project, test runner, and application environment.

faq.question: Can it help with flaky tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on deterministic waits, stable selectors, isolated data, network control, and useful failure artifacts.

faq.question: Is it safe for production environments?
faq.answer: The skill warns against destructive tests in production. Use dedicated test accounts, local services, or controlled staging environments.

faq.question: Does it cover accessibility or visual regression testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for accessibility scans, visual snapshots, browser projects, and CI artifact capture.
